newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - March 21.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - March 21.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - A disciplined, buy-it-as-you-need-it approach on the purchasing and left most lumber items within their recent narrow trading ranges, Random Lengths said in its weekly review. Framing lumber prices finsihed the week mixed but with a slight bias to the downside, the lumber reporting agency said.

A burst of shortcovering developed after Tuesday's strong housing starts report sent May futures up the limit, but the action quickly cooled. In most areas, lumber moved briskly out of dealers' yards whenever a few days of dry weather allowed jobsites to dry out. But many buyers remained on the fence.

The debate over how much Canadian lumber will cross the border after April 1 was a major contributor to this cautious attitude. Canadian producers argued that their order files and stocks were in check, but some secondaries still saw enough downward pressure building to sell short. Reports of distressed loadings and reload offerings at some producers were also cited.

Uncertainty also surrounded the volume of Canadian inventory in the field. Reports ranged from "skimpy" to "ample." Confusion over what percentage of existing stocks was already sold just compounded the uncertainty, Random Lengths said.
Canadian lumber exports as of March 12 were at 97.1 percent of annual fee-free quota for the year ending March 31.

Many of the rail cars hung up in transit during the past two months were finally getting unloaded. But some producers in the West continued to report shipping problems ranges from car shortages to poor car-size selection. Also, more flooding in Washington state forced at least one cedar mill to halt output.
A break in the rainy pattern in the South Central region gave mills there hope that they will see more logs, along with more sales to nearby buyers, Random Lengths said.
